title: Budgeted Chaos Curriculum for Platform Operators
author: Maya Patel
content:
Title: Budgeted Chaos Curriculum for Platform Operators

Introduction
This document describes a structured training curriculum and exercise library for platform operators focused on "budgeted chaos" — controlled fault injection and degradation experiments designed to validate SLO preservation, fallback behavior, cost-signal integrity, and safe operator responses while constrained by a simulated or real cost budget. The goal is to make chaos exercises repeatable, measurable, and safe for production-adjacent environments.

Scope and intent
- Scope: multi-tenant inference runtime and adjacent services (runtime-router, batcher, kv-prefix-cache, quota-guard, cost-signal-fanout, autoscaler).
- Intent: reduce surprise during cost and capacity shocks; ensure operator playbooks and automated mitigations behave under explicit cost constraints.
- Out-of-scope: full-scale destructive chaos that violates customer SLAs without explicit executive signoff.

Audience
- Platform operators and oncall engineers (primary)
- SREs, runtime engineers, incident commanders (secondary)
- Trainer / hiring interviewers for operator role (tertiary)

Learning objectives
After completing the curriculum, participants will be able to:
1) Design and run a budgeted chaos experiment plan that exercises fallback model swaps and regional failover without exceeding a predefined token-cost budget.
2) Use the exercise templates to assert success criteria (SLOs, cost delta, error rates) and populate postmortem artifacts.
3) Operate the telemetry and dashboards required to triage cost-related regressions and forward actionable remediation to product and infra teams.
4) Execute rollback and safe-degrade procedures that preserve high-priority customer SLOs under budget pressure.

Curriculum overview (modules)
- Module 1 — Foundations (1 day)
  - Concepts: budgeted chaos rationale, risk classification, safety cages.
  - Tools: chaos-driver (internal CLI), experiment-config repo, telemetry sandbox, cost-signal-fanout viewer.
- Module 2 — Observability & Telemetry (half day)
  - Dashboards to know: Token cost attribution, per-route latency/99th, prefix-cache hit profile, quota-guard counters.
  - Alerts and thresholds (see "Monitoring and Alerts" section).
- Module 3 — Experiment Design (half day)
  - Plan templates, success/failure criteria, preflight checklist.
- Module 4 — Hands-on Exercises (2 days)
  - Run 3 canonical exercises in a staging region that simulates production tenants with scaled-down traffic and a token-cost budget.
- Module 5 — Postmortem & Roadmap (half day)
  - Postmortem template, metric collection, and targeted followups for runtime, billing, and product.

Exercise blueprints (canonical library)
Each exercise blueprint contains: purpose, services involved, preflight checks, experiment steps, monitoring queries, success criteria, rollback steps, and postmortem prompts. Use the experiment-config template (JSON) below to instantiate.

1) Token-surge with model-swap (cost-bounded)
- Purpose: Validate automated model-fallback and model-variant routing when a tenant suddenly generates a token surge and the preferred model is rate-limited or exceeds performance/cost thresholds.
- Services: runtime-router, model-catalog, quota-guard, autoscaler, cost-signal-fanout.
- Preflight checks:
  1. Confirm test tenant traffic replay is enabled (test-tenant id: tt-budgeted-chaos).
  2. Ensure a dedicated tenant budget in quota-guard is set to 100k tokens for the run window.
  3. Verify canary model variant (gptx-small-q4) is available in the same region.
- Steps:
  1. Set quota-guard budget to 100k tokens for tenant tt-budgeted-chaos.
  2. Use chaos-driver to replay traffic with synthetic prompt mix (40% long-context, 60% short).
  3. At t+2m, inject a 50% slowdown on preferred model backends using kernel-throttle toggle.
  4. Observe routing: runtime-router should divert >80% requests to model-variant within 30s, respecting token budget.
- Monitoring queries and dashboards:
  - Token cost attribution (dashboard id: dash-token-cost-001)
  - runtime-router reroute rate (metric: router.reroute.rate)
  - Model latency p95/p99 (metric: model.latency.{model_name}.p99)
- Success criteria:
  - No customer-facing 5xx spike > 0.1% above baseline in the test window.
  - Token consumption does not exceed 100k budget.
  - Fallback model maintains p99 <= 1.5x of baseline.
- Rollback:
  - Stop replay. Re-enable original backend. Confirm traffic returns to baseline within 90s.
- Postmortem prompts:
  - Was routing decision observable within the dashboard?
  - Any billing signal drift?

2) Regional capacity budget exhaustion (simulated)
- Purpose: Validate cross-region routing and degraded-mode behavior when a region reports capacity exhaustion while a global token budget prevents immediate burst provisioning.
- Services: smart-router, capacity-orchestrator, regional-autoscaler, cache-prefetch, s3-prefill (for warmup).
- Key thresholds:
  - Region capacity alarm: available_gpus < 5
  - Failover window target: route < 500ms additional latency
- Steps (high level):
  1. Preflight: create region-limited budget in capacity-orchestrator with 10% of normal headroom.
  2. Execute synthetic region storm for region us-west-2 with chaos-driver.
  3. Observe smart-router rebalancing; verify cost-aware routing avoids regions flagged as "expensive" until budget refresh.
- Success criteria:
  - Critical tenant SLOs (SLO: 99th latency < 1.2s for high-priority routes) held for at least 95% of requests.
  - No uncontrolled cross-region egress cost > $150 above baseline during run.

3) KV prefix-cache evictions and warmup lag
- Purpose: Exercise graceful degradation when KV prefix cache (kv-prefix-cache) evicts hot entries and cold-cache penalties occur.
- Services: kv-prefix-cache, batcher, prefix-warmup agent, runtime-router.
- Observability pointers:
  - cache.hit_rate.primary_prefix
  - cache.eviction.rate (per-minute)
  - warmup.latency.p95
- Success criteria:
  - Warmup agent reduces cold-call latency by 40% within 2 minutes of observed eviction spike.

Experiment-config template (JSON example)
- Use this template in repository experiments/canary-configs. Replace placeholders with real test tenant and budget values.
{
  "experiment_name": "token-surge-model-swap-budgeted-2027-01",
  "tenant": "tt-budgeted-chaos",
  "budget_tokens": "100000",
  "duration_minutes": "20",
  "injection_profile": "mixed-context-long-short",
  "safety_cage": {
    "max_customer_error_increase_pct": "0.1",
    "abort_on_cost_overrun": "true"
  }
}

CLI snippets
- Launch experiment (staging):
  $ chaos-driver run --config ./experiments/token-surge-model-swap.json --env staging --simulate-cost true
- Abort experiment:
  $ chaos-driver abort --id <experiment-id>

Monitoring and alerts (baseline thresholds)
- Immediate operator alerts (page):
  - Token budget overrun: quota-guard.budget.remaining_pct < 10% within experiment window.
  - Model-fallback-failure: router.reroute.failed.count > 5 in 1m
  - Eviction storm: cache.eviction.rate > 500/min for 5 min
- Dashboard panels to review during run:
  - Token consumption by tenant and route
  - Per-model p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput
  - Reroute rate and failed reroutes
  - Cost-signal drift by region and hour

Preflight checklist (must be signed by experiment owner)
1) Experiment config validated in experiments repo and peer-reviewed.
2) Test tenant exists and is isolated from production customer traffic.
3) Required dashboards (token-cost, model-latency, router-reroute) are pinned on the operator console.
4) Oncall rotation notified (email + Slack #ops-chaos).
5) Rollback / abort playbook verified for the run window.

Operator runbook extract (condensed)
1) Pre-run: run the preflight checklist. Confirm budget and telemetry.
2) Start: issue chaos-driver run and mark the experiment in the journal channel.
3) Observe: first 10 minutes are the safety window. If any immediate page fires, follow incident runbook and abort.
4) Mid-run: execute predetermined manual checks at t+5m and t+12m.
5) End-run: stop replay, run validation queries, collect artifacts (traces, dashboards snapshots, experiment logs).
6) Postmortem: complete experiment postmortem template within 48 hours.

Postmortem template (fields)
- Summary (one sentence)
- Timeline (minute-resolution)
- Observed metrics vs expected
- Root cause and contributing factors
- Action items (owner + ETA)
- Learning and recommended platform changes

Training schedule and recommended cadence
- Quarterly full curriculum run for each oncall cohort.
- Monthly short drills (1-hour tabletop) focusing on one blueprint.
- After any production token-cost incident, run immediate revalidation within two weeks.

Ownership and escalation
- Curriculum owner: Platform Enablement (owner: Maya Patel, contact: maya@redwood.ai).
- Exercise steward: runtime-team oncall (rotation document: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/oncall-rotation).
- Executive escalation: Head of Platform (if experiment risk classification is "level 3" or higher).

Measuring effectiveness
- Suggested KPIs to track across cohorts:
  - Mean time to detect fallback failure during exercises (target < 2m)
  - Fraction of exercises where token budgets were respected (target 100%)
  - Number of action items closed within SLA after postmortem (target 90% within 30 days)

Appendix: Safety cage definitions and risk classification
- Risk level 1: Low — staging-only, simulated cost, no route to production. Requires experiment owner signoff.
- Risk level 2: Medium — production-adjacent (mirrored traffic), bounded budget, requires peer reviewer + SRE lead approval.
- Risk level 3: High — production impacting; requires head of platform and legal signoff.

Appendix: Useful queries
- token_cost_by_tenant: sum(token_cost) by tenant, 5m
- model_latency_p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- router_reroute_rate: rate(router_reroute_total[1m])

Related resources

- Operator training slides: /drive/platform/training/budgeted-chaos-2027.pdf
